abstract: N-methyl-D-aspartate receptor (NMDAR) antibody encephalitis is a recently described immunotherapy-responsive panencephalitis with characteristic features that include a psychiatric onset and a later movement disorder. This entity was first described as a paraneoplastic phenomenon in young women with ovarian teratomata. However, more recently it has become clear that the majority of patients, particularly children, do not harbor a tumor and that males can also be affected. With the development of the NMDAR antibody assay, now available worldwide, a few patients with classical limbic encephalitis and early psychosis and epilepsy have also been found to harbor these antibodies. Early diagnosis followed by immunotherapies and tumor removal, when relevant, expedite recovery from the condition. Antibody levels correlate with the clinical severity of the disease in individual patients, and the antibodies have been shown to substantially reduce NMDA receptors on hippocampal neurons both in vitro and in vivo, supporting the likely direct pathogenicity of the NMDAR antibodies.
abstract_ja: N-メチル-D-アスパラギン酸（NMDA）受容体抗体脳炎は、免疫療法が有効な汎脳炎であり、精神症状で発症し、後に運動障害を呈するという特徴を持つ。この疾患は当初、若年女性の卵巣奇形腫に伴う傍腫瘍性現象として報告された。しかし近年、多くの患者、特に小児では腫瘍を伴わないこと、また男性も発症しうることが明らかになった。NMDAR抗体検査が世界的に利用可能になったことで、古典的な辺縁系脳炎や早期精神病・てんかんを呈する症例にも、これらの抗体が見つかるようになった。早期診断と免疫療法、ならびに必要に応じた腫瘍摘出により回復が促進される。抗体価は個々の患者の臨床的重症度と相関する。この抗体はin vitroおよびin vivoで海馬ニューロンのNMDA受容体を大幅に減少させることが示されており、NMDAR抗体の直接的な病原性が示唆される。
